quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily spots, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less grip than normal pavement.

questions.question: When riding, keeping space around your motorcycle helps you to:

options.text: Have time to react to dangers.
Look at road signs more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to dangers.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This space gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need the space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing while riding, even during the day, to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol levels or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding to increase your chances of being seen, even during the day.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When riding in a group:

options.text: The group should have at least nine riders.
Split into two or more smaller groups if you have more than four or five riders.
Large groups will not get separated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Split into two or more smaller groups if you have more than four or five riders.
questions.explanation: Small groups are safer than large groups. Small groups are easier for other drivers to pass, less likely to get separated, and riders do not have to rush to keep up. Split large groups into smaller groups if you have more than four or five riders.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip wearing a jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding for protection, even in warm weather. A jacket helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces to prevent them from catching on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, decrease your speed. Sudden movements on a slippery surface can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system even if you drink one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Lay the motorcycle down before hitting an obstacle.
Wear a helmet that is fastened securely.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash. You should also wear eye protection and protective clothing.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one that puts you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where you can see others and they can see you. Avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your riding ability?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually they won't affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding ability. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks, loose padding, or other damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no damage like cracks or loose padding. Style does not matter for safety.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. Stop safely and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous place for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most conflicts between riders and other drivers.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your eyes as well as a face shield does.
Your face as well as a windshield does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield is better because it protects your whole face. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks still in the system.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding?

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.
